headline: High-risk git/workspace overlap from Aider’s write+git defaults; injection and leakage are lower but real, while B’s sparse profile limits confidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and edits repo files and can execute shell commands, so malicious content in shared files can influence its prompts or tool use. nuwa-skill has no documented ingestion path, but the pair shares a repo-style interaction surface through Aider’s shared git workspace, making prompt injection plausible though not proven.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill writes attacker-controlled text into files Aider later reads, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents operate on the same repository checkout, shared-file prompt injection is enabled.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different working copies.
Require human review of any file content Aider ingests as instructions.
Strip or quarantine untrusted text before Aider reads it.
Use a read-only mirror for nuwa-skill inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file-originated instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and has broad network egress, so sensitive repo data can leave the workspace if it is sent to configured model providers. nuwa-skill’s profile is sparse, but the pair still creates a default shared-workspace leakage path through Aider’s file access and outbound API calls.
conditions: IF the shared repository contains secrets or private source code, Aider can expose them to external model providers.
IF nuwa-skill and Aider share the same checkout, file contents can be read by Aider and transmitted outward.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared repo before running either agent.
Use a redacted branch for Aider.
Restrict Aider’s model-provider configuration to approved endpoints.
Run nuwa-skill in a separate workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce content filtering before outbound prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem, modify git state, and supports multiple instances via a shared git repo. nuwa-skill’s write surface is undocumented, so uncertainty does not reduce the risk; the shared mutable repo makes concurrent edits and git-state conflicts dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same repository or branch, concurrent git conflicts can occur.
IF nuwa-skill also writes to the shared workspace, overwrite races become possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Disable auto-commit for one agent during overlap.
Review and merge changes manually after each run.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can produce code changes and git commits, and nuwa-skill is a scientific-research agent with no documented verification barrier. If nuwa-skill consumes Aider’s outputs as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect downstream actions or commits, though the profile does not prove direct automation.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill treats Aider-generated edits or summaries as ground truth, errors can propagate.
IF Aider commits changes that nuwa-skill later reuses without verification, cascading failure is enabled.
mitigations: Require explicit verification before nuwa-skill consumes Aider output.
Add a diff-review step for every Aider commit.
Limit Aider to draft-only changes.
Log provenance for each downstream artifact.
requires-engineering: implement automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider explicitly handles model-provider API keys and can send repo content to configured providers, while nuwa-skill has no documented residency or retention constraints. The pair therefore has a compliance gap only if regulated data is placed in the shared workspace; the evidence is one-sided, so the other agent is not cited beyond its sparse profile.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared repo, Aider may transmit it to external providers.
IF organizational policy requires local-only processing, Aider’s configured egress violates that policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo.
Use a local-only model configuration for Aider.
Document retention and deletion expectations before use.
Run nuwa-skill on non-sensitive datasets.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for outbound prompts.
